9: Panel-first, then genome-wide, then a designed submission. (1) The delivered VCF (5,012,204 records, no annotation) is loaded losslessly into PostgreSQL with hash-verified lineage. (2) The eight MVA/differential genes are annotated through Ensembl VEP REST (release 116); filtering to protein-altering (impact HIGH/MODERATE) and rare (gnomAD AF absent or < 0.01) leaves exactly two alleles, both in BUB1B, both heterozygous PASS. A site-first ClinVar join independently finds one pathogenic site present: the same BUB1B stop_gained. (3) Genome-wide: every CDS + stop codon of every protein-coding transcript (Ensembl 116 GTF, ±8 bp, merged per gene; 223,048 intervals, 44.6 Mb) is range-joined to the callset → 38,087 distinct coding alleles, all VEP-annotated (191 requests, checkpointed) → 875 rare protein-altering → 65 genes biallelic on PASS calls → exactly 1 with a ClinVar-pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank: BUB1B. (4) A panel-blind phenotype ranker (Exomiser's human-phenotype path re-implemented in Python over HPO release 2026-06-23, reading no DNA) ranks BUB1B 6/5,267 on the child's seven own terms; joined to the 65 biallelic genes it is first by a wide margin. (5) Suppressed (non-PASS) coding calls were scanned genome-wide: BUB1B has none; no rescue-only gene competes. (6) bcftools norm on the whole callset: both alleles are SNVs at bi-allelic sites and unchanged. (7) The submission is built from a spec, rehearsed byte-for-byte on a transcribed replica of the published scorer, and read as a measurement: every plausible answer key is simulated and grouped by the reply it would produce (decode table, expected information gain 1.46 bits). Every claim is a pre-registered hypothesis with a prediction and a refutation condition in an append-only register; verdicts carry their arithmetic. Full report and code: https://github.com/agharsallah/mva-hackathon (submissions/track1/iteration-1/).
10: Automated to the ranked gene table and the candidate pair (results.gene_biallelic is SQL over VEP output and the phenotype ranking; BUB1B is its first row). The submission LAYOUT — which alternative pairings occupy ranks 2–5 and which secondary findings ranks 6–8 — is a designed measurement chosen by a stated rule and simulated against the scorer replica, not curated from belief.
11: None on the candidate itself. Manual steps: choosing the rarity cutoff (0.01, recessive) and the impact classes before any run; writing the hypothesis space and priors for the decode table (stated in the report); selecting secondary-finding rows by a fixed rule (ClinVar P/LP after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes). LLM assistance (Anthropic API, Claude) was used to write code and documentation; no LLM judged a variant.
13: Ensembl release 116 gene models (GTF) and VEP REST (GRCh38) with gnomAD v4 genome/exome frequencies, ClinVar classifications, and the SpliceAI, AlphaMissense and CADD plugins for the two candidate alleles; ClinVar GRCh38 VCF (fileDate 2026-08-29) for the site-first join; gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics; HPO release 2026-06-23 (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype) for the phenotype ranking; UCSC hg38 analysis-set FASTA (chr prefix stripped) for normalization; PubMed (PMID 15475955, 20516114, 31184400, 18548531). Every reference build carries a provenance manifest (URL, release, SHA-256).
15: Pairs. Every primary row is a compound-heterozygous pair in one row (chrom_1/pos_1 + chrom_2/pos_2). The pipeline ranks genes by biallelic sets and the submission is built pair-first; single-variant rows are used only as secondary findings.
16: Rows 6–8 are marked finding_type=secondary: a heterozygous LZTR1 stop_gained (ClinVar P/LP, gnomAD 1.4e-6; dominant schwannomatosis predisposition, unrelated to MVA), Factor V Leiden (F5, heterozygous, low-penetrance risk factor) and a heterozygous FLG stop_gained (ichthyosis vulgaris). Rule: ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic after excluding conflicting and benign-tagged records, gnomAD AF < 0.02, dominant or risk-factor genes; recessive carrier states (GNRHR, CIAO1, ZFYVE26) are reported in the report but not submitted. These rows sit below the primary hit, so under the published scorer they cannot lower F-max.
17: About one hour of wall clock on one laptop: coding-interval build 5 s; coding layer derivation ~17 min (pulling 5 M rows over the network); genome-wide VEP annotation ~33 min at 4 concurrent requests (free Ensembl REST); gene table 24 s; normalization 15 s; figures and submission build < 2 min. Cost: none beyond a small hosted PostgreSQL (~5 €/month). No alignment of the 160 Gb of reads was needed.
18: We identify the causal compound-heterozygous pair for a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy as two BUB1B alleles: a stop_gained already classified pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1 in ClinVar (exon 17 of 23, gnomAD 3.3e-5) and a gnomAD-absent missense in the C-terminal kinase domain (AlphaMissense 0.92, CADD 24.5). Four instruments converge: a panel filter (VEP rarity × consequence leaves exactly these two alleles), a site-first ClinVar join (one pathogenic site present in the callset — the same stop), a genome-wide coding scan (38,087 annotated alleles, 65 biallelic genes, exactly one with a pathogenic allele and a top-30 phenotype rank), and a symptom-only ranking that never read the DNA (BUB1B 6th of 5,267). Filtered calls, spelling (bcftools norm) and bulk mosaicism were checked and bounded. The genotype matches the established MVA1 mechanism (one null allele plus one hypomorph leaving reduced BubR1; Hanks 2004, Suijkerbuijk 2010), and rhabdomyosarcoma is a reported MVA malignancy. Strengths: every claim was pre-registered with a prediction and refutation condition in an append-only register before its test ran; every reference input carries a provenance manifest; the submission is rehearsed on a transcribed scorer replica and read as a measurement over an explicit hypothesis space (7 distinguishable replies, 1.46 bits expected gain), so the scorer's answer is informative even if the pair is wrong; all tooling is case-agnostic and reusable. Limitations: the genome-wide scan is coding-only (CDS ± 8 bp, 1.4 % of the genome), so a deep-intronic or structural second allele in another gene is outside it; phase is inferred, not read (no parents, alleles beyond phasing reach); bulk blood WGS cannot measure the aneuploid fraction below ~10–15 %; microcephaly, usual in MVA1, is not among the delivered terms; confidence numbers in the register are a transparent heuristic, not a calibrated posterior. Runtime ~1 h on a laptop with free public APIs.
